children: Motiva Enterprises began restarting its small crude distillation unit (CDU) at its 656,400 barrel-per-day (bpd) Port Arthur, Texas, refinery on Thursday, according to people familiar with plant operations.

The 90,000-bpd unit was among several shut on Tuesday night as Tropical Storm Eduoard passed near the refinery, the largest in the United States, the sources said. VPS-2 is the smallest of the refinery's three crude distillation units.
Motiva did not reply to a request for comment.
CDUs typically mark the first stage of the refining process, breaking crude oil into feedstocks used by other processing units.
The restart of VPS-2 returns all units shut by the storm to production at the refinery.

The restarted units include the 81,000-bpd gasoline-producing fluidic catalytic cracking unit, the 57,000-bpd delayed coker-1, 18,000-bpd alkylation unit, the 49,000-bpd catalytic reformer-4, and MPU-3, which produces lubricating oil.
Cokers convert residual crude oil from distillation units into either feedstock for motor fuels or petroleum coke, a coal substitute.
Alkylation units and reformers use different processes to produce octane-boosting components used to make premium blends of gasoline.
